title: What happened at the Seattle airport? Outrage as ICE arrests man and daughter boarding flight
summary: A chaotic scene unfolded at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport Saturday as a father and daughter were detained by masked immigration officers while boarding their flight bound for L.A.

blocks.text: World·New
A chaotic scene unfolded at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport Saturday as a father and daughter were detained by masked immigration officers while boarding their flight bound for L.A.
ICE says both had overstayed their visas
'They're taking my dad:' Masked ICE agents arrest passengers at Seattle airport
It's been described as "horrific," "chilling" and "distressing."

A chaotic scene unfolded at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday morning as a father and daughter were detained by masked immigration officers while boarding their flight at around 8 a.m. PST.

Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles recorded the struggle, which showed two men in unmarked jackets and khaki pants struggling with someone on the ground as onlookers screamed, cried and a woman shouted: "They're taking my dad."
The men "just lunged forward. They didn’t identify themselves and then sort of hit this family from behind," said passenger John Gaedeke, who filmed part of the confrontation.
The videos have since gone viral.
Lawmakers and other officials have decried the arrests, and protesters have been marching through the airport chanting "ICE out now."
A person argues with a police officer during a protest at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday. (David Ryder/Reuters)
So, what happened? Why did Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrest the father and daughter? And what happens to them now? Here what to know:
Who was arrested?

ICE officers conducted an operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, the agency said in a statement posted on social media, and also arrested, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, later identified as Mendoza's daughter.

A lawyer for them both says they were travelling to attend a baptism ceremony in California and have been seeking asylum in the U.S., where they have lived since 2015. They have no criminal record, said Olia Catala.

blocks.text: "They’ve done everything correctly, and these are educated people," Catala said.
Mejia "went to college, to university, she worked for a nonprofit," she said. "So it’s just heartbreaking."

Catala told local media that Mendoza brought his daughter to the U.S. when she was 14, and that they entered legally on tourist visas. Mendoza later filed an asylum claim, the attorney told NBC-affiliate King5 News, and Meija married a U.S. citizen and filed paperwork for adjustment of her status.
"The entire family is traumatized," she told King5 News.

People react as ICE officers detain passenger on the jetbridge for an Alaska Airlines flight from Seattle to Los Angeles in this screengrab from a video obtained from social media and verified by Reuters. (John Gaedeke/Reuters)
Mejia’s husband was accompanying Mejia and her father when they were arrested, Catala said, but was not detained.
"This is a family whose lives have been turned upside down," Catala said Sunday in a statement posted to social media.
Both are being held at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Catala said.
Why were they arrested?
The "targeted" operation was to arrest Mendoza, ICE said in a statement, describing him as "an illegal alien from Mexico" who had overstayed his visa.

ICE has stepped up arrests at airports since the summer, especially targeting people it says have overstayed visas. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said it no longer tolerates "aliens in our country illegally to jet around our country."
"This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport," DHS said in a statement to CBC News.

ICE said that, during the Saturday morning arrest, other travellers began to "obstruct and assault" the officers, and claims that one passenger "hurled hot coffee" at them. They identified her as Mejia, also calling her "an illegal alien from Mexico with visa overstay."

Video shared with @komonews shows part of the arrests made by masked ICE agents on a jet bridge at @flySEA this morning. The Port of Seattle said it was “outraged” by the incident and investigating. #seattle (Video: John Gaedeke) https://t.co/t6J6csdZ0R—clairecweber
ICE said Meija "will be charged with assaulting a federal officer."
Catala, their attorney, says Meija was holding a cup of coffee during the confrontation, but disputes that she threw it. Other passengers who witnessed the scene said it was knocked out of her hands.
"When somebody’s charging at you, you’re going to drop a cup of coffee," Catala said. "There was a lot of panic, chaos, not knowing what’s going on."
People protest at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport Saturday. (David Ryder/Reuters)
What's the reaction?
In addition to the public backlash and protests, lawmakers and other officials have decried the arrests.

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson called the videos "horrific" and "chilling," and Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said she was "outraged" by the sight of masked ICE agents "causing chaos and dragging a woman off the jetway."
"ICE is completely and totally out of control and today we are confronted with yet more evidence of this," Ferguson told a news conference on Saturday.
"These tactics are unacceptable and un-American," Wilson said in a statement posted on social media.

blocks.text: Washington Attorney-General Nick Brown also decried the arrests, writing on social media: "We are sick and tired of poorly trained masked federal agents vanishing people out of thin air.
"Washingtonians will never accept these stunts as legitimate or responsible law enforcement."
The Port of Seattle said in a statement it was "outraged" by the incident, adding that immigration enforcement at the airport are conducted without the port’s participation or knowledge.
"This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred."
Alaska Airlines also said it wasn't provided advanced notice and that it was "concerned."
April Sims, president of the Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, called the ICE arrest a "smash-and-grab" action that injected fear and chaos during a delicate time for air travel.
The union includes local chapters representing flight attendants and ground crew at the airport.
A screengrab from a video obtained from social media, verified by Reuters, shows the scene on the jetbridge Saturday. (John Gaedeke/Reuters)
